evidence: Cic. Fin. 2.27: rādīcitus tollere atque extrahere cupiditātem (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Literally, roots and all (weeds pulled up by Cato); so of a change that goes to the root. Latin says it with the verb: a radical change is rādīcitus mūtāre, not an adjective with a noun.

evidence: Cic. Off. 1.35: Carthāginem et Numantiam funditus sustulērunt (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: From fundus, the bottom: of destroying or changing something completely.

phrases.latin: Hunc mōrem nōn paulātim sed rādīcitus mūtāre volunt.
phrases.english: They want to change this custom not gradually but radically.

sources: Lewis & Short: radicitus · Lewis & Short: funditus
